newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary 1996 budget deficit 3.3 pct of GDP - govt.
newsitem.headline: Hungary 1996 budget deficit 3.3 pct of GDP - govt.

text.p: Hungary's 1996 budget deficit was 3.3 percent of the country's gross domestic product (GDP), a government official said on Thursday.
"The budget deficit was 3.3 percent of the GDP," government spokesman Elemer Kiss told a news conference following the weekly government meeting.
He added that the 1996 current account deficit was between $1.5 to $1.6 billion forints.
Kiss also said that the central budget deficit was 100 billion forints less than expected, mainly due to higher than expected revenues from corporate tax payments.
The original budget deficit target for 1996 was 233 billion forints.
Hungary's budget deficit was a cumulative 111.1 billion forints for the January-November period of 1996.
Kiss said that the 1996 social security deficit was 55 billion forints higher than the originally planned 17.8 billion forints.
Hungary last March signed a standby loan agreement with the International Monetary Fund in which the country undertook to keep the overall state budget below four percent of the GDP.

Finance Ministry officials said in December that the higher-than-expected social security gap would probably be offset by better-than-planned corporate tax revenues and one-off revenues of some 34 billion forints.
